updates.previous: Minimum 10% equity injection required; up to half can be a seller note on full standby
updates.proposed: Minimum 15% equity injection required for deals over $500k; seller notes no longer count toward equity injection (even on full standby)
updates.reason: New lender guidance indicates a shift: equity requirement has increased from 10% to 15%, and seller notes are no longer credited at major SBA lenders. This eliminates a key lever for reducing cash requirements.

updates.previous: SBA 7(a) with 10% buyer equity (up to half as seller note on full standby) and 80–90% SBA loan.
updates.proposed: SBA 7(a) with 15% buyer equity (all cash; seller notes no longer credited) and 85% SBA loan. For a buyer with $120k liquid capital, this constrains viable deal size to ~$800k.
updates.reason: The seller note strategy (full standby credit toward equity) is no longer viable at this lender. Equity injection is now 15% all-cash, which significantly reduces the deal-size ceiling relative to liquid capital.

updates.section: first_steps → [action: deal calculator and ceiling setting]
updates.previous: Your deal-size ceiling is 10–20x your liquid capital (e.g., $75k liquid = $750k–$1M deal).
updates.proposed: With $120k in liquid capital and a non-negotiable 15% all-cash equity requirement (no seller note credit), your deal-size ceiling is approximately $800k ($120k ÷ 0.15). This is ~6.7x your liquid capital, not 10–20x.
updates.reason: New lender requirement: 15% equity injection with zero seller note credit. This is a hard constraint that binds tighter than the previous 10% assumption with seller note flexibility.

updates.previous: Equity injection (buyer cash, minimum) | $50,000–$100,000 for a $1M deal (5–10% depending on seller note)
updates.proposed: Equity injection (buyer cash, minimum) | $120,000 required (15% non-negotiable; zero seller note credit). This fixes deal-size ceiling at approximately $800k and exhausts your liquid capital.
updates.reason: The equity injection is now 15% all-cash with no seller note offset. Your $120k cash directly determines your maximum deal size at $800k.

updates.previous: Set ceiling at 10–20x your liquid capital after the audit
updates.proposed: Set ceiling at $800k hard stop, given 15% equity requirement and zero seller note credit. Do not anchor higher until you confirm whether other SBA lenders accept seller notes.
updates.reason: This lender's 15% all-cash-only rule is binding for your $120k capital base. Before committing sourcing effort to larger deal sizes, shop other SBA PLP lenders to see if they still accept seller notes; if they do, you may access larger deals elsewhere.

updates.proposed: NEW BLOCKING QUESTION: Are other SBA Preferred Lender Program lenders still accepting seller notes toward equity injection at 10%, or has the industry shifted to 15% all-cash-only across the board? This determines whether your plan must target $800k deals or whether you can shop for lenders with more flexible terms.
updates.reason: One major lender now requires 15% with zero seller note credit. If this is standard across SBA lenders, your plan is constrained to $800k. If other lenders are still accepting 10% with seller note credit, you retain flexibility to target larger deals. Must resolve in Phase 1 lender conversations.
